source.title: Towards Biologically Plausible Convolutional Networks
source.authors: Roman Pogodin; Yash Mehta; T. Lillicrap; P. Latham

page_placements.theme: Architectural inductive biases must match the task

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares convolutional and locally connected image classifiers and tests whether dynamic weight sharing or translated-image repetitions recover convolutional performance. This is a conceptual test of V3's architectural-bias and local-connectivity components; it does not compare against fully connected networks.
record.gate_note: The study tests trained image classifiers on natural image datasets and reports test accuracy for convolutional and locally connected networks under several regularization conditions. The paper's cited comparisons with earlier studies are not extracted as results.
record.test_reason: The study compares convolutional networks with locally connected networks, including variants with dynamic weight sharing. It has no fully connected comparator, so it cannot establish V3's convolutional-versus-fully-connected advantage or how much of that advantage local connectivity explains. Its own results do not test any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that translation repetitions are costly and leave a performance gap, whereas dynamic weight sharing brings locally connected networks near convolutional accuracy and improves correspondence to ventral-stream data. They argue this supports convolutional networks as neuroscience models. The classifier experiments implement the proposed sleep phase by directly averaging weights, rather than simulating the full Hebbian dynamics.
record.recipe_differences: Both use gradient-trained image classifiers, but the study compares convolutional networks with locally connected networks, adds translated-image repetition or dynamic weight sharing, and uses AdamW. It does not use fully connected networks or measure training-versus-test error gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, padding/available translations, and dynamic weight-sharing frequency change the performance gap; on ImageNet, the authors also state the trade-off depends on learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: With local connectivity retained, removing weight sharing lowers held-out accuracy: CIFAR10 80.9% versus 88.3%, CIFAR100 49.8% versus 59.2%, TinyImageNet 29.6% versus 38.6%, and ImageNet 46.7% versus 63.5% top-1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convolutional weight sharing improves image-classification accuracy over otherwise locally connected ResNet variants in these training settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Translation repetitions improve locally connected classifiers but leave a gap; frequent dynamic weight sharing approaches convolutional performance and exceeds the TinyImageNet reference in some metrics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dynamic weight sharing can recover much of the accuracy lost when convolutional layers are replaced with locally connected layers; recovery depends on sharing frequency and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Using a convolutional first layer improves the ImageNet dynamic-sharing models; sharing every batch gives 63.6% top-1 and 84.5% top-5 versus the convolutional reference's 63.5% and 84.7%.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A convolutional first layer can further improve locally connected ImageNet classifiers trained with dynamic weight sharing.

record.problems: ImageNet results are single runs. The reported comparisons are between convolutional and locally connected networks, not fully connected networks; accuracy comparisons do not measure the train-test generalization gap. Small-scale runs report means over 5 runs and max-min ranges, rather than standard errors or confidence intervals.
record.rows_left_out: None. The extracted Table 1 and Table 2 results and additional ImageNet results in Appendix Table 13 fit within the 60-row limit.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label generalization under the same recipe, and chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.

Convolutional versus fully connected test error; the contribution of local connectivity to that advantage; learning sparse local connections from fully connected networks; initialization from trained convolutional networks.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning-dependent differences.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a batch-size penalty.
Dropout effects and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization gaps and competing measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All states are cannot_determine relative to the listed versions; the reported accuracy differences remain interpretable for the separate claims in fits_no_version. Related-work statements about fully connected networks are cited findings, not this study's results. Appendix Tables 4 and 6 also report padding-0 and padding-8 results, and Table 13 includes an unshared hybrid baseline omitted from the record; these do not test a listed version. Small-scale uncertainties are max-minus-min ranges over five runs; ImageNet results are single runs. Reported table differences can differ from subtraction of rounded displayed accuracies.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Fully connected networks trained from scratch; learned sparse local connections; convolutionally initialized fully connected networks; MNIST and SVHN.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum SGD.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout and its interaction with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.
